title: 1000 Layer Networks for Self-Supervised RL: Scaling Depth Can Enable New G

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states: 'Note additionally that the parameter count scales linearly with width but quadratically with depth.' This is backwards. For a fixed hidden size, increasing depth adds layers linearly, so parameters scale linearly with depth. Increasing width (hidden size) makes each layer's weight matrix grow quadratically, so parameters scale quadratically with width. The statement should say the parameter count scales linearly with depth and quadratically with width.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3 vs Figure 9 caption and Appendix B.6 hyperparameters
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Section 3 defines the critic as a dot product: f_{φ,ψ}(s, a, g) = φ(s, a)^⊤ ψ(g). However, Figure 9 caption computes Q as L2 distance: Q(s, a, g) = ‖φ(s, a) − ψ(g)‖_2. The hyperparameter table in Appendix B.6 lists 'energy_function: L2'. This contradicts the dot-product definition and creates confusion about how the critic is actually parameterized.

The text states: 'g_j represents a goal sampled from a different, random trajectory' and the denominator is a sum over j=1..K of e^{f(s_i,a_i,g_j)}. This excludes the positive goal g_i from the denominator. The standard InfoNCE loss (Sohn 2016) includes the positive sample in the softmax denominator. The description either misrepresents the actual loss or uses a non-standard loss without clarification.

The title reads: '1000 Layer Networks for Self-Supervised RL: Scaling Depth Can Enable New G' which appears truncated. The abstract states the full purpose as 'New Goal-Reaching Capabilities'. The discrepancy suggests an incomplete title in the submitted document.
